theme: Feudal Japan: Samurai, Shogunate & Sengoku Era
title: Feudal Japan: Samurai, Shogunate & Sengoku Era
description: A 60-question grand master assessment on the Kamakura and Tokugawa shogunates, Samurai bushido code, Oda Nobunaga, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and Edo period culture.

questions.question: Who established the Kamakura Shogunate in 1192 CE, becoming the first official Shogun of feudal Japan?
questions.explanation: Minamoto no Yoritomo defeated the Taira clan in the Genpei War, establishing the Kamakura Bakufu and initiating warrior dominance over the imperial court.

questions.question: What war between the Taira and Minamoto clans between 1180 and 1185 established the dominance of the samurai warrior class?
questions.explanation: The Genpei War culminated in the naval Battle of Dan-no-ura in 1185, where the Minamoto decisively crushed the rival Taira clan.

questions.question: What term was used for the military government of Japan headed by a shogun from 1192 to 1867?
questions.explanation: Bakufu translates literally as tent government, reflecting the battlefield origins of military administration.

questions.question: Which aristocratic court era preceding the rise of the samurai was renowned for cultural refinement, The Tale of Genji, and the Heian-kyo capital?
questions.explanation: The Heian Period in Kyoto celebrated classical aesthetics and literature while delegating regional policing to provincial warrior clans.

questions.question: Which Buddhist sect emphasizing direct intuition, meditation, and mental discipline became deeply embraced by samurai warriors?
questions.explanation: Zen Buddhism appealed to samurai through its emphasis on calm focus, detachment from mortality, and rigorous self-discipline.

questions.question: In what year CE did Emperor Go-Toba formally grant Minamoto no Yoritomo the title of Sei-i Taishogun, founding the Kamakura Shogunate?
questions.explanation: In 1192 CE, Yoritomo was appointed Shogun, establishing hereditary military governance that lasted nearly seven centuries.

questions.question: What ethical and philosophical code of conduct, meaning Way of the Warrior, governed samurai behavior, loyalty, and honor?
questions.explanation: Bushido synthesized Confucian loyalty, Zen detachment, and Shinto martial spirit, emphasizing honor, courage, and self-sacrifice.

questions.question: What specialized high-purity carbon steel produced in traditional tatara clay smelting furnaces was used to forge katana blades?
questions.explanation: Tamahagane steel was forged by smelting iron sand and charcoal over three days, producing metal of variable carbon content for blade lamination.

questions.question: What ritual form of suicide by disembowelment did samurai perform to restore family honor or avoid capture?
questions.explanation: Also known as harakiri, seppuku allowed a warrior to demonstrate courage, dying with honor alongside an appointed second who delivered decapitation.

questions.question: What paired set of swords, consisting of the long katana and short companion wakizashi, symbolized samurai social status?
questions.explanation: The Daisho, literally big-small, was an exclusive badge of samurai nobility throughout the feudal era.

questions.question: What distinct curved polearm weapon with a single-edged blade was famously mastered by samurai women of the bushi class and warrior monks?
questions.explanation: The naginata provided superior reach and sweeping cuts, making it a favored defense weapon for onna-musha female warriors.

questions.question: Approximately how many total layers of steel are created in a masterfully folded traditional Japanese katana blade during forging?
questions.explanation: Folding a steel billet 15 successive times doubles the grain structure repeatedly, producing 2^15 or 32,768 micro-layers of steel.

questions.question: What natural weather disaster destroyed the invading Mongol-Yuan fleets in 1274 and 1281, inspiring the term Divine Wind?
questions.explanation: Massive typhoons battered Kublai Khan's armada in Hakata Bay, saving Japan and giving rise to the spiritual belief in Kamikaze.

questions.question: What massive coastal defensive fortification did the Kamakura shogunate build along Hakata Bay to repel the second Mongol invasion?
questions.explanation: The Genko Borui was a 20-kilometer stone wall erected along the Kyushu coast, preventing Mongol landing forces from establishing a beachhead.

questions.question: Which regent clan held de facto political control over the Kamakura Shogunate through the position of Shikken?
questions.explanation: The Hojo clan governed as hereditary regents for figurehead shoguns, successfully repelling the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281.

questions.question: What brief imperial restoration in 1333 led by Emperor Go-Daigo sought to abolish military rule before being overthrown?
questions.explanation: The Kenmu Restoration attempted to reassert direct imperial rule, but disillusioned samurai rallied behind Ashikaga Takauji.

questions.question: Who turned against Emperor Go-Daigo and established the Ashikaga Muromachi Shogunate in Kyoto in 1336?
questions.explanation: Ashikaga Takauji drove Go-Daigo to Yoshino and established his new military administration in the Muromachi district of Kyoto.

questions.question: In what year CE did the second and largest Mongol invasion armada under Kublai Khan assault the coast of Kyushu?
questions.explanation: The 1281 invasion fleet carried an estimated 140,000 Mongol, Chinese, and Korean troops before being devastated by typhoons.

questions.question: Which famous Zen temple in Kyoto, covered in gold leaf, was built by Ashikaga Shogun Yoshimitsu in 1397?
questions.explanation: Kinkaku-ji, the Temple of the Golden Pavilion, exemplifies the luxurious Kitayama cultural style patronized by Ashikaga Yoshimitsu.

questions.question: What stylized classical theatrical art form, characterized by wooden masks and slow movements, was perfected under Ashikaga patronage by Zeami?
questions.explanation: Zeami Motokiyo refined Noh drama into a philosophical spiritual art form blending Zen principles, poetry, and masked dance.

questions.question: What devastating civil conflict in Kyoto from 1467 to 1477 shattered the Ashikaga Shogunate and initiated the Warring States period?
questions.explanation: The Onin War erupted over shogunal succession disputes, reducing Kyoto to ashes and initiating a century of decentralized civil warfare.

questions.question: What era of continuous civil war and social upheaval, lasting from 1467 to roughly 1603, is known as the Country at War period?
questions.explanation: During Sengoku Jidai, regional warlords known as daimyo fought continuously for territorial dominance and national supremacy.

questions.question: What title was given to the powerful feudal lords who commanded private samurai armies and governed autonomous provincial domains?
questions.explanation: Daimyo, meaning great name, ruled castle towns and commanded vassal retainers during the feudal era.

questions.question: For how many total continuous years did the destructive Onin War ravage Kyoto between 1467 and 1477?
questions.explanation: The Onin War lasted ten grueling years, destroying the political authority of the Ashikaga bakufu and triggering Sengoku anarchy.

questions.question: Who was the first of the Three Great Unifiers of Japan, known for his ruthless pragmatism and adoption of firearms?
questions.explanation: Oda Nobunaga unified central Japan through economic liberalization, military modernization, and crushing religious warrior bastions.

questions.question: In what pivotal 1560 battle did Oda Nobunaga achieve a stunning surprise victory against the vastly superior army of Imagawa Yoshimoto?
questions.explanation: Nobunaga exploited a torrential rainstorm to launch a flank attack on the resting Imagawa command, instantly catapulting to prominence.

questions.question: In which 1575 battle did Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu deploy rotating volleys of matchlock arquebuses behind wooden palisades to crush Takeda cavalry?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Nagashino demonstrated the lethal superiority of synchronized firearm volley fire over traditional mounted samurai charges.

questions.question: What Portuguese matchlock firearm, introduced to Japan via a shipwrecked trade vessel in 1543, revolutionized Sengoku warfare?
questions.explanation: Named after the island of Tanegashima where it arrived, Japanese metalsmiths rapidly reverse-engineered and mass-produced thousands of matchlocks.

questions.question: At which Kyoto temple was Oda Nobunaga betrayed and forced to commit seppuku by his general Akechi Mitsuhide in 1582?
questions.explanation: The Honno-ji Incident cut short Nobunaga's unification campaign just as he stood on the verge of total military mastery.

questions.question: How many matchlock arquebuses did Oda Nobunaga famously deploy in triple-ranked rotating volleys at the Battle of Nagashino in 1575?
questions.explanation: Nobunaga deployed 3,000 arquebusiers behind wooden palisades, maintaining continuous fire that decimated the famed Takeda cavalry.

questions.question: Who rose from humble peasant origins to succeed Oda Nobunaga and become the second Great Unifier of Japan?
questions.explanation: Toyotomi Hideyoshi avenged Nobunaga at Yamazaki, subjugated the remaining daimyo, and completed the political unification of Japan.

questions.question: What nationwide decree did Toyotomi Hideyoshi enact in 1588 to disarm the peasantry and enforce rigid social class segregation?
questions.explanation: The Sword Hunt confiscated all weapons from farmers, declaring the metal would be melted to construct a giant Great Buddha statue.

questions.question: What grand golden castle did Toyotomi Hideyoshi build as his primary power base and fortress in western Japan?
questions.explanation: Built in 1583 on the former site of the Ishiyama Hongan-ji, Osaka Castle was an impregnable fortress with massive granite walls.

questions.question: What master tea ceremony practitioner developed the wabi-cha rustic tea aesthetic under the patronage of Oda Nobunaga and Hideyoshi?
questions.explanation: Sen no Rikyu established the timeless principles of harmony, respect, purity, and tranquility before being ordered by Hideyoshi to commit seppuku.

questions.question: What ambitious foreign military campaign did Toyotomi Hideyoshi launch twice in the 1590s in an attempt to conquer Ming China?
questions.explanation: The Imjin War (1592-1598) devastated the Korean peninsula before Japanese forces withdrew following Hideyoshi's death.

questions.question: In what year CE did Toyotomi Hideyoshi launch his first massive invasion armada of over 150,000 samurai into Joseon Korea?
questions.explanation: Launched in 1592, the initial Japanese campaign made rapid early gains before encountering Joseon naval resistance and Ming Chinese intervention.

questions.question: Which decisive battle fought on October 21, 1600, secured Tokugawa Ieyasu's undisputed mastery over Japan?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Sekigahara pitted Ieyasu's Eastern Army against Ishida Mitsunari's Western Army, ending in a crushing Tokugawa triumph.

questions.question: Which general defected mid-battle from the Western Army at Sekigahara, attacking his own allies and ensuring Tokugawa victory?
questions.explanation: Kobayakawa Hideaki withheld his troops until pressured by Tokugawa gunfire, charging down Mount Matsuo to crush the Western flank.

questions.question: What historic castle town did Tokugawa Ieyasu choose as the administrative capital of his shogunate, later renamed Tokyo?
questions.explanation: Ieyasu transformed the swampy fishing village of Edo into a colossal fortified administrative center and the world's most populous city.

questions.question: In what two-part siege in 1614 and 1615 did the Tokugawa Shogunate finally eliminate the Toyotomi clan and burn Osaka Castle?
questions.explanation: The Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka eliminated Toyotomi Hideyori and established unchallenged Tokugawa supremacy.

questions.question: Which famous warrior, known as the Crimson Demon of War, led legendary suicidal cavalry charges against Tokugawa headquarters at Osaka?
questions.explanation: Sanada Yukimura fought with such ferocity at the Summer Siege of Osaka that Tokugawa Ieyasu praised him as the number one warrior in Japan.

questions.question: Approximately how many total combatants fought across the misty fields at the Battle of Sekigahara in October 1600?
questions.explanation: Roughly 160,000 soldiers from across Japan clashed at Sekigahara in the largest and most consequential samurai battle in history.

questions.question: What system of alternate attendance forced daimyo to reside in Edo every other year and leave their families as hostages?
questions.explanation: Sankin-kotai drained daimyo financial resources through costly annual processions, preventing rebellion and centralizing shogunal control.

questions.question: What was the strict four-tier Confucian social class hierarchy established during the Edo period called?
questions.explanation: Shinokosho ranked society into Samurai (warriors), Farmers (producers), Artisans (makers), and Merchants (traders) at the bottom.

questions.question: What term was used for a masterless samurai who had lost his lord or domain due to warfare or shogunal confiscation?
questions.explanation: Ronin roamed the countryside as mercenaries, teachers, bandits, or bodyguards during peacetime.

questions.question: What white plaster fortress in Hyogo prefecture, nicknamed the White Heron Castle, survived centuries of warfare intact?
questions.explanation: Himeji Castle is Japan's finest surviving feudal castle, featuring intricate defensive gates, stone drops, and an eight-story main keep.

questions.question: Which legendary dual-wielding swordsman and philosopher authored The Book of Five Rings on martial strategy?
questions.explanation: Miyamoto Musashi fought over 60 undefeated duels, developing the Niten Ichi-ryu two-sword technique before retiring to write philosophy.

questions.question: For how many total years did the peaceful Tokugawa Edo Shogunate rule Japan between 1603 and 1867?
questions.explanation: The Pax Tokugawa maintained internal peace and stable military governance for 264 years until the Meiji Restoration.

questions.question: What strict foreign policy of national seclusion, enacted in the 1630s, banned foreigners and forbade Japanese from leaving abroad?
questions.explanation: Sakoku restricted foreign interactions to eliminate Christian influence and monopolize foreign trade through strictly controlled ports.

questions.question: What artificial fan-shaped island in Nagasaki harbor served as the sole trading post for Dutch merchants during the Sakoku era?
questions.explanation: Dutch traders were confined to Dejima, serving as Japan's sole window to European scientific and medical knowledge known as Rangaku.

questions.question: What covert agents, trained in espionage, stealth, sabotage, and guerrilla tactics in Iga and Koga, served feudal warlords?
questions.explanation: Shinobi performed covert reconnaissance, infiltration, and intelligence gathering throughout the feudal era.

questions.question: What popular dynamic theatrical art form featuring dramatic makeup, elaborate costumes, and all-male actors flourished during the Edo period?
questions.explanation: Created by Izumo no Okuni, Kabuki evolved into vibrant urban entertainment beloved by the rising merchant class in Edo and Osaka.

questions.question: What genre of Japanese woodblock prints and paintings, meaning pictures of the floating world, depicted geishas, actors, and landscapes?
questions.explanation: Ukiyo-e prints by master artists like Hokusai and Hiroshige captured the ephemeral pleasures and landscapes of Edo urban life.

questions.question: In what year CE did the bloody Shimabara Rebellion of Christian peasants and ronin lead to the complete sealing of Japan under Sakoku?
questions.explanation: The 1637 Shimabara Rebellion led by teenage rebel Amakusa Shiro prompted the Shogunate to outlaw Christianity and ban Portuguese trade.

questions.question: What celebrated historical incident in 1703 involved 47 former samurai who avenged their master Lord Asano before committing ritual seppuku?
questions.explanation: The Ako incident exemplified ultimate samurai devotion, inspiring the classic theatrical play Chushingura.

questions.question: Which American naval commodore sailed four black-hulled steam warships into Edo Bay in 1853, demanding Japan open to foreign trade?
questions.explanation: Commodore Matthew Perry's Black Ships forced the signing of the Treaty of Kanagawa in 1854, ending two centuries of national isolation.

questions.question: What historic transformation in 1868 abolished the Tokugawa Shogunate, returned supreme power to Emperor Meiji, and ended the samurai era?
questions.explanation: The Meiji Restoration dismantled feudal domain privileges, created a conscript national army, and modernized Japan into an industrial power.

questions.question: Which southern samurai leader led the 1877 Satsuma Rebellion, the final armed resistance of traditional samurai against the imperial government?
questions.explanation: Saigo Takamori led thousands of disaffected samurai in Kyushu, dying in battle on Shiroyama and becoming a legendary folk hero.

questions.question: What 1876 imperial decree forbade the public wearing of samurai swords, officially marking the end of warrior class privileges?
questions.explanation: The Haitorei decree prohibited all citizens except military personnel and police from carrying swords in public, dissolving the samurai caste.

questions.question: In what year CE did the Meiji Restoration occur, formally dissolving the centuries-old shogunate system and restoring imperial rule?
questions.explanation: In 1868, the last Shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu stepped down, initiating rapid modernization and industrialization under the Meiji Emperor.
